long_biography.plain_text:
Rice began practicing law in 1979 after earning business and law degrees from the University of South Carolina. Working with trial lawyer Ron Motley, he developed a complementary role as the negotiator who structured resolutions while colleagues prepared cases for court. His work on asbestos claims and the landmark tobacco settlement established his reputation in large-scale civil litigation.

In 2003, Rice and Motley founded Motley Rice, which grew into one of the United States' largest plaintiffs' litigation firms. Rice has since helped negotiate settlements involving the BP oil spill, vehicle emissions, prescription opioids and other mass torts. He remains active as a founding member and national co-lead counsel, and his philanthropy has endowed scholarships, professorships and legal training at the University of South Carolina.
